recipes.name: Pumpkin Pasta
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for serving

steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Once the water is boiling, stir in the penne, and return to a boil. Cook the pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the pasta has cooked through, but is still firm to the bite, about 11 minutes. Drain well in a colander set in the sink.

Heat the pumpkin puree, chicken broth, milk, margarine, onion powder, black pepper, salt, cloves, nutmeg, cinnamon, and ginger in a large skillet over low heat until heated through, about 5 minutes. Stir in the drained pasta, and toss with the Parmesan cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Pumpkin puree is turned into a creamy, smooth sauce with just a hint of cloves, nutmeg, and cinnamon. Toss with whole wheat pasta and Parmesan cheese, and you've got a kid-pleasing meal in under 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I made this tonight and with a few minor tweaks, mine turned out fabulous! My advice: START WITH A ROUX as others have suggested. I melted some butter, sauteed diced garlic and onion, added some flour, and then whisked in the broth and milk (I used equal parts broth and milk - makes it more creamy). Add pumpkin and bring to a simmer. I didn't want mine to taste like pumpkin pie, so instead of the cloves and cinnamon, I added white pepper and cayenne pepper. These two really rounded out the savory flavor and gave it just a hint of heat. Also, plenty of grated parmesan cheese! I didn't want to stop eating it. Will definitely make again.

I changed my mind 15 times about making this for dinner. I finally decided, "what the heck..." I DID make the roux with a tablespoon each of butter and flour but otherwise stuck right to the recipe. It was very creamy with a nice, light pumpkin flavor. I served it up with a couple of links of my homemade hot sausage. Best meal of the week!

Cheap and easy. Didn't have onion powder so fried up 1/4 onions. Did as other reviewers suggested and used a rue base (2 tbs butter and flour). Used two cups small pasta, one cup frozen vegetables and half a brick of extra firm tofu.

Gave it 5 stars after quite a few changes. For sauce I melted 2 T. butter and sauteed a small ch. onion and 2 ch. garlic cloves until onion was soft. Then I added 1 T. flour and cooked it for around 1 min. Then I whisked in 1 C. chick. broth, 1 C. fat free 1/2 & 1/2 and 1 C. pumpkin. Then I added 1/2 t. ground ginger, 1/2 t. sage, around 1/4 t. cinnamon. I did not add cloves. I let it simmer for around 10 min. just until it was the thickness I wanted. I added in some cooked ch. pumpkin spice chicken sausauge. I grated parmesan cheese over pasta after it was on our plates.

This was great! I modified the recipe after reading other reviews. I used 2 Tbsp. butter instead of margarine and made a roux from 1/3 red pepper, 1/2 vidalia onion, 2 cloves garlic (all minced)and 1 tbsp. flour. I added 1 c. each of half&half, chicken broth and pumpkin puree and let simmer on low-medium for about 10-15 minutes until sauce was nice and thick. I used more savory spices: nutmeg, sage, thyme, ginger, black pepper, cayenne pepper, (about 1/4 tsp. each-- a little more ginger and sage for my taste) to taste, and a pinch of ground cloves I added the 1/4 cup parmesan cheese. The last few minutes of cooking I added grilled chicken breast 1 cup diced (you can add more if you like.) I served over whole wheat rotini pasta...yum!

I made this treat for my wife who I knew really wouldn't like it 'soupy,' so I changed the recipe in the area of chicken broth, nonfat milk, and margarine. 

I made a roux of 2 tbsp melted butter, 2 tbsp flour, and 1/2 cup whole milk; cooked it a couple of minutes to thicken, then added the pumpkin and continued heating while mixing it well. Then I added only enough chicken broth to get the consistency I wanted. All of the seasonings were added as suggested in the recipe. 

I joking call my wife a 'food snob' because she really likes flavorful food, and plain dishes DO NOT get a favorable review. This Pumpkin Pasta was a HIT! She really liked it! Definitely will make again.

This is SUPER easy and so YUMMY! 
I did make a few slight changes... I started with a roux, as suggested by a few others. I also used fresh onions(instead of powder) and fresh pumpkin puree. -Super simple to make, btw... Cut a pumpkin in half, take out the seeds, place it face down and bake it for about an hour @ 350. Then you just scoop out the innards and put them in your food processor or blender. Voila!!
I also added a handful of baby 'bello mushrooms and some fresh rosemary. SUPER YUMMY!! Thank you for sharing!

I made a roux first as others have suggested and used the recipe more as a guide instead. To start, I fried some bacon, added a little butter, then onions, garlic, celery and diced bellpeppers. Once the veggies are fragrant, I coated them in flour. I used evaporated milk to start making the roux. I also saved a cup of pasta water in advance and dissolved a boullion cube while it was still hot, then poured it slowly to the roux. And I added grated parmesan and quezo de bola (ball of cheese). Once I got to the consistency I liked, I mixed in the pureed pumpkin. I thinned the sauce down with some water, then seasoned with salt and pepper to taste. I saved some of the celery leaves as garnish.

Delicious! I’ve made this several times now, and like some other reviewers, I prefer to make it more savory by omitting the cinnamon, cloves and nutmeg. I’ve also found that starting out with a roux with the butter and flour before adding the rest of the ingredients, makes the sauce creamier.
Delish, and the family loved it!! Used chili powder, paprika and chipotle spices instead to give it a kick. Also started with a roux as reviews suggested.. Definitely would make again

Recipe was amazing. Started out blan but added a few spices. As others stated, I started with a roux to make the sauce thick and less soupy. I sautéed onions, garlic, carrots, and 1 small sweet pepper and then added some cornstarch to make a nice roux. I then added low sodium chicken stock, pumpkin, and soy cream. For the seasonings I used salt, pepper, garlic powder, pinch of nutmeg, pinch of cinnamon, cayenne pepper, fresh parsley, a pinch of sage and ALOT of parmesean cheese. I served it over wheat bow tie pasta. Really really good. Next time I think I will add roasted chicken or some type of chicken sausage.

I found this recipe to be of good use for leftover pumpkin. It wasn’t great as the taste was just so so. My husband ate it and so did I but it does need something. I think the sauce was enough for 8 oz of noodles I guess it depends on if you want your noodles swimming in sauce or just covered in sauce, 6oz of noodles made the sauce a bit too much.
I like this recipe. It's a great way to have pumpkin in the fall. I added cream cheese and spinach.
Made it but had no onion powder. Had pumpkin flavor, but just felt bland like it needed something extra

Love this! Very simple . I followed the recipes almost exactly, just used a store-bought graham-cracker crust and added a bit more cream cheese. The pumpkin flavoring is very subtle. I also experimented by putting an Oreo cookie in the bottom of a muffin liner and put cream cheese fillings on top. That worked great too.
Different tasting for me. I felt it needed some extra spice. Maybe cause I used more pasta then it required but the kids enjoyed it which is a success for me.
I wasn't crazy about it.

Moving this recipe into my meal rotation & will repeat without changes to the recipe. It has the pumpkin pie spices without the sweetness normally associated with pie. Would definitely be good to serve to a child.

I give this 3 stars for ease of preparation, nutrition and the fact that it is fairly inexpensive to make. I followed the advice of others and made a roux which gave it a nice texture. As for the taste, the seasoning just didn’t meld for me. I tried to salvage it by adding more but it just didn’t work. I won’t be making this again, but I will continue to search for similar recipes.
Dish turned out well. Not a fan of Parmesan cheese, but I substituted for shredded cheese. Tasted really good and easy to make!
